subject: Physics
chapter: Newton's Laws of Motion and Friction

raw.questionText: A wedge of inclination angle $\theta = 45^\circ$ is accelerated horizontally to the left with a constant acceleration $a$. A block of mass $m = \sqrt{2}\text{ kg}$ is placed on the inclined surface of the wedge. The coefficients of static and kinetic friction between the block and the wedge are $\mu_s = 0.5$ and $\mu_k = 0.4$, respectively. Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
options: If $a = 2\text{ m/s}^2$, the friction force acting on the block is $4.8\text{ N}$ and its acceleration relative to the wedge is $1.6\sqrt{2}\text{ m/s}^2$.
If $a = 5\text{ m/s}^2$, the friction force acting on the block is $5\text{ N}$ directed downwards along the incline.
If $a = 20\text{ m/s}^2$, the friction force acting on the block is $10\text{ N}$ directed downwards along the incline.
If $a = 40\text{ m/s}^2$, the friction force acting on the block is $20\text{ N}$ and its acceleration relative to the wedge is $5\sqrt{2}\text{ m/s}^2$.
raw.explanation: Analyze the transition from static to kinetic friction by finding the range of acceleration for which the block remains stationary in the non-inertial frame of the wedge.
